notes: Governmental-immunity/premises-defect case about a long-term public-housing tenant's slip-and-fall; addresses licensee/invitee duty under the Tort Claims Act, not the character or regulation of short-term letting.
Oil-and-gas mineral lease and Relinquishment Act dispute among life tenants and remaindermen; no residential letting or lodging issue.
Premises-liability case about a newspaper carrier's invitee status at an apartment complex; does not address the letting of rooms/dwellings.
Premises-liability slip-and-fall involving a relative helping with a household move; invitee/licensee analysis unrelated to compensated letting.
Premises-liability case about a child injured in a private office building; invitee analysis, no letting or lodging issue.

holding_summary: Owners who built single-family dwellings on subdivision lots per the restrictive covenants were held entitled to rent those dwellings, since the restrictions did not expressly bar one owner from renting multiple houses he owned. The court reversed the trial court and dissolved an injunction that had treated such renting as an impermissible business use in violation of the deed restrictions.

quotes.text: Real estate restrictions must be strictly construed resolving all doubt in favor of the free and unrestricted use of the property.
It is undisputed all the houses are single family dwellings, and that owners in the addition have the right to rent their dwellings.

notes: Court does not use lease/license/lodging/innkeeping vocabulary to characterize the tenancies -- only addresses validity of restrictive covenant as applied to renting -- so characterization left null.
Zoning dispute over a fraternal lodge's commercial bingo operation; unrelated to residential letting or lodging-house regulation.

holding_summary: A restrictive covenant limiting a subdivision to single-family residential use is not violated by renting rooms merely incidental to use of the main dwelling, but is violated when an owner rents a separate structure on the premises, such as a garage apartment, as a source of financial gain. Because the Foxworths rented their garage apartment to Rice University students for $45 to $85 per month, the court reversed the denial of an injunction and rendered judgment enjoining them from renting the garage apartment as a source of financial gain.

quotes.text: the renting of a room or rooms in a private residence, which is merely incidental to its use as a family residence, does not violate a restriction limiting the use of the property to a single-family residence.

If the evidence establishes as a matter of law, or if the trial court finds as a fact on conflicting evidence or as a reasonable inference from the evidence, that a particular defendant is . using an establishment on his premises, separate and apart from his dwelling house, for renting as a source of financial gain that activity should be enjoined.

It was uncontradicted that the Foxworths received $85 each month as rental on the garage apartment (an establishment on the premises, separate and apart from the dwelling house), and that approximately $6 per month was spent on the utilities for the garage apartment.

notes: Insurance-coverage dispute over whether a company was a 'borrower' or 'lessee' of a delivery truck under an auto policy's omnibus clause; unrelated to residential letting.

holding_summary: The court held that resubdividing a corner lot into two separately titled structures violated deed restrictions requiring buildings to front the platted street with reserved rear easements, and that renting the rear structure to unrelated tenants while the front structure was used as a family residence violated the covenant prohibiting multiple family housing. The court voided the subdivision conveyances, ordered the lots reunified, and enjoined renting any structure apart from the family dwelling as a separate housekeeping unit.

quotes.text: No apartment house or duplex will be permitted in the addition; the object of this provision being to prohibit multiple housing throughout the entire addition.

Summary judgment evidence showed that appellant Carol Finkelstein rented out the two-story wooden frame building to two young women not related to her or to each other, a clear violation of the prohibition against multiple family housing.

enjoins defendants from renting or leasing any structure on the original lot apart from defendants' dwelling house to anyone, or from renting space to others in defendants' dwelling house as a separate housekeeping unit, "it being the express purpose of this Order and Decree that the sole use of the Original Lot be limited to that of a single family residency."

notes: Zoning/nuisance dispute over horse-racing and gambling ordinances at a private racetrack; no letting or lodging issue.

holding_summary: The court held that a nuisance-closure order under the Alcoholic Beverage Code may reach only the portion of a building where the violations actually occurred; because the ground-floor pool halls, not the owner-operated Rose Hotel on the second floor, were the site of the liquor-code violations, closing the entire building was an abuse of discretion. The physically separate hotel, where the owner and his common-law wife lived and rented remaining rooms to the public, was excluded from the closure and the case was remanded.

quotes.text: The second floor of the building, containing sixteen rooms, is a hotel where Locke and his common law wife live. They operate the hotel, renting the remaining rooms to the public.
The second floor should not have been closed, however, because there is no evidence of Code violations on that floor.

notes: Primary holding is about the scope of nuisance-closure orders under the Alcoholic Beverage Code, not about letting rights per se; hotel facts are background but the court's treatment of the owner-run hotel as a distinct, unaffected lawful enterprise is mildly favorable.

Hotel Occupancy Tax dispute over whether banquet/meeting rooms in a separate building count as taxable 'hotel' occupancy; construes statutory hotel/lodging-house definitions in passing but does not adjudicate the legality or character of letting/lodging arrangements themselves.
Zoning/police-power challenge to an auto-wrecking-yard fencing ordinance; unrelated to residential letting.

Invasion-of-privacy tort case against a motel over an employee's interference with registered paying guests' room; turns on vicarious-liability/managerial-capacity issues, not the character of the letting arrangement.
Fire-insurance coverage dispute over whether insureds' second house was 'occupied' under a policy clause; involves the insureds' own dual residences, not letting to another for compensation.
Zoning/liquor-license distance-from-residential-district dispute; unrelated to letting or lodging of dwellings.
Oil-and-gas mineral preferential-purchase-right and rule-against-perpetuities dispute; unrelated to residential letting.
